I am a PhD candidate in Education Policy at the University of Virginia and an Institute of Education Sciences (IES) pre-doctoral fellow. I study new technologies in schools, asking two questions: **do they actually help students**, and **can we trust the data we use to decide?**

My dissertation takes on both. One chapter evaluates a tutoring program that combines adaptive software with live virtual tutors, developing a method for extending credible causal estimates from the narrow group where they are cleanest to the full population a district actually serves. Another asks when scores produced by AI language models can be trusted to measure human behavior — using classroom observations of teachers as the test case — and provides a framework for choosing among AI scoring systems before deploying them.

Though my applications are in education, both problems are general: any field adopting new technology has to estimate effects beyond where the evidence is strongest, and increasingly has to decide whether AI-generated measurements are reliable enough to act on. I build statistical software in Stata/Mata and work in R and Python.
